## Guides
### How to get a Canada work permit from Uzbekistan
URL: https://riskllc.us/guide-canada-work-permit-uzbekistan.html (RU: https://riskllc.us/ru/guide-canada-work-permit-uzbekistan.html, UZ: https://riskllc.us/uz/guide-canada-work-permit-uzbekistan.html)
Answer: Most citizens of Uzbekistan get a Canada work permit by first receiving a genuine job offer from a Canadian employer, usually supported by a positive Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) or an LMIA-exempt offer number. You then apply online to IRCC, pay the CAD 155 work permit fee plus CAD 85 for biometrics, and give fingerprints at a visa application centre. Real employers never charge you for a job offer.
Fees: Work permit: CAD 155 per person; Biometrics: CAD 85 (CAD 170 for a family); Open work permit holder fee (e.g. eligible spouses): CAD 100; Employer compliance fee (paid by the employer, not you): CAD 230
Q: Can I get a Canada work permit without a job offer? A: Usually not. Open work permits exist only for specific groups, such as eligible spouses of some workers and students or graduates of Canadian schools. Most people from Uzbekistan need an employer-specific permit based on a job offer.
Q: How long does a Canada work permit take? A: It depends on the country you apply from and changes weekly. Check the current time for Uzbekistan in IRCC's official processing times tool before you plan your trip.
Q: Can a work permit lead to Canada PR? A: Yes. After at least 1 year (1,560 hours) of skilled paid work in Canada within 3 years, you may qualify for the Canadian Experience Class through Express Entry, or for a Provincial Nominee Program.
Q: Someone offers me a Canadian job for money. Is it real? A: Be careful. IRCC warns that job offer scams are common. Employers must not charge you for an LMIA or a job offer.
Sources: https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/fees/fees.asp, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/permit/temporary.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/foreign-workers.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/protect-fraud.html

### Canada visitor visa: requirements and documents
URL: https://riskllc.us/guide-canada-visitor-visa-requirements.html (RU: https://riskllc.us/ru/guide-canada-visitor-visa-requirements.html, UZ: https://riskllc.us/uz/guide-canada-visitor-visa-requirements.html)
Answer: Citizens of Uzbekistan need a Canada visitor visa (temporary resident visa) to visit. You apply online, pay CAD 100 plus CAD 85 for biometrics, and must show a clear purpose of travel, enough money for the trip and strong ties that will bring you home. The border officer decides how long you may stay, usually up to 6 months.
Fees: Visitor visa: CAD 100 per person (max CAD 500 per family of 5+); Biometrics: CAD 85 per person, CAD 170 per family; Biometrics are generally valid for 10 years
Q: How much money do I need for a Canada visitor visa? A: IRCC does not publish a fixed amount. You must show enough money for your stay and return trip, with a normal account history. Large unexplained deposits hurt your case.
Q: What is the super visa? A: Parents and grandparents of Canadian citizens or permanent residents can apply for a super visa, which allows stays of up to 5 years per visit, with extra requirements such as medical insurance and an invitation from the child or grandchild.
Q: Why are Canada visitor visas refused? A: Common reasons are weak ties to your home country, unclear purpose, or finances that do not match the trip. You can reapply with stronger documents.
Sources: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada.html, https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/fees/fees.asp, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/campaigns/biometrics.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html

### US B1/B2 tourist visa from Uzbekistan: DS-160, interview and fee
URL: https://riskllc.us/guide-us-b1-b2-visa-uzbekistan.html (RU: https://riskllc.us/ru/guide-us-b1-b2-visa-uzbekistan.html, UZ: https://riskllc.us/uz/guide-us-b1-b2-visa-uzbekistan.html)
Answer: To get a US B1/B2 visa from Uzbekistan you complete the online DS-160 form, pay the $185 non-refundable application fee and attend an interview at the US Embassy in Tashkent. At the interview you must show that your trip is temporary and that strong ties will bring you back home. A separate $250 visa integrity fee created by a 2025 US law may be charged when a visa is issued, so check the Embassy's current instructions.
Fees: Visa application (MRV) fee for B1/B2: $185, non-refundable; Visa integrity fee: $250 under a 2025 law, collected at issuance where implemented; confirm with the Embassy; As of Oct 2026 Uzbekistan is not on the US visa bond country list
Q: Do I need an interview for a US tourist visa? A: Interviews are generally required, with limited exceptions, and the consular officer can require an interview from anyone. Most first-time applicants from Uzbekistan attend an interview in Tashkent.
Q: What does a 214(b) refusal mean? A: The officer was not convinced your visit is temporary or that you qualify. You can reapply when your situation or evidence has changed; a new fee is required.
Q: How long can I stay on a B1/B2 visa? A: The CBP officer at the airport decides and records it on your Form I-94. Visa validity and permitted length of stay are different things; overstaying voids your visa.
Sources: https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/tourism-visit/visitor.html, https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/fees/fees-visa-services.html, https://ceac.state.gov/genniv/, https://uz.usembassy.gov/visas/, https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/global-visa-wait-times.html

### UK Standard Visitor visa from Uzbekistan
URL: https://riskllc.us/guide-uk-visitor-visa-uzbekistan.html (RU: https://riskllc.us/ru/guide-uk-visitor-visa-uzbekistan.html, UZ: https://riskllc.us/uz/guide-uk-visitor-visa-uzbekistan.html)
Answer: Citizens of Uzbekistan need a Standard Visitor visa to visit the UK for tourism, family or business for up to 6 months. You apply online on gov.uk no earlier than 3 months before travel, pay £135, and give fingerprints and a photo at a visa application centre. A decision usually comes within 3 weeks.
Fees: Standard Visitor visa (6 months): £135; 2-year long-term visa: £506; 5-year long-term visa: £903; 10-year long-term visa: £1,128
Q: Can I work in the UK on a Standard Visitor visa? A: No. You can do permitted activities like tourism, visiting family and attending business meetings, but not paid or unpaid work for a UK company.
Q: Do I need a TB test for a UK visitor visa? A: Only if you are visiting for more than 6 months, for example on a medical or academic visitor visa.
Q: Will I get a refund if refused? A: No. The fee is not refunded if your application is refused or you get a shorter visa than requested.
Sources: https://www.gov.uk/standard-visitor/apply-standard-visitor-visa, https://www.gov.uk/standard-visitor, https://www.gov.uk/check-uk-visa, https://www.gov.uk/faster-decision-visa-settlement

### F-1 US student visa: step by step
URL: https://riskllc.us/guide-f1-student-visa-steps.html (RU: https://riskllc.us/ru/guide-f1-student-visa-steps.html, UZ: https://riskllc.us/uz/guide-f1-student-visa-steps.html)
Answer: To get an F-1 visa you must first be accepted by a SEVP-certified US school, which issues your Form I-20. You then pay the $350 SEVIS I-901 fee, complete the DS-160, pay the $185 visa fee and attend an interview at the US Embassy in Tashkent. New students can get the visa up to 365 days before classes start but may enter the US no more than 30 days before the start date.
Fees: SEVIS I-901 fee (F-1): $350; Visa application (MRV) fee: $185; Visa integrity fee: $250 under a 2025 law, collected at issuance where implemented; confirm with the Embassy
Q: Can I work on an F-1 visa? A: Only in limited ways: on-campus jobs within limits, and practical training such as CPT or OPT with authorization. Unauthorized work breaks your status.
Q: Can I study on a tourist visa instead? A: No. Study toward a US degree or certificate is not allowed on a B visa, even for a short program.
Q: Do my spouse and children need visas? A: Yes, they apply for F-2 visas with their own I-20s from your school; they do not pay the SEVIS fee.
Sources: https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/study/student-visa.html, https://www.ice.gov/sevis/i901, https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/school-search, https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/fees/fees-visa-services.html, https://uz.usembassy.gov/visas/

### Canada Express Entry PR explained
URL: https://riskllc.us/guide-canada-express-entry-pr.html (RU: https://riskllc.us/ru/guide-canada-express-entry-pr.html, UZ: https://riskllc.us/uz/guide-canada-express-entry-pr.html)
Answer: Express Entry is Canada's online system for skilled-worker permanent residence through the Federal Skilled Worker Program, the Canadian Experience Class and the Federal Skilled Trades Program. You create a profile, get a Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score, and the highest-ranked candidates receive an invitation to apply for PR. After you become a PR, you can apply for Canadian citizenship once you have been physically present for at least 1,095 days in the last 5 years.
Fees: PR application incl. right of PR fee: CAD 1,590 per adult (CAD 990 + CAD 600); Dependent child: CAD 270; Biometrics: CAD 85 (CAD 170 per family); Proof of funds (FSW/FST, updated July 2025): CAD 15,263 for 1 person, CAD 19,001 for 2, CAD 28,362 for 4; Citizenship application later: CAD 653 per adult
Q: Do I need a job offer for Express Entry? A: No. A job offer is not required for most candidates, and since March 25, 2025 job offers no longer add CRS points. A provincial nomination still adds a large number of points.
Q: Who does not need proof of funds? A: Candidates invited under the Canadian Experience Class, and those authorized to work in Canada with a valid job offer.
Q: What is the minimum CRS score? A: There is no fixed minimum. Each draw has its own cut-off, which changes from draw to draw and by category. Check recent rounds on canada.ca.
Q: How soon can I become a Canadian citizen? A: After becoming a permanent resident, you need at least 1,095 days of physical presence in Canada in the 5 years before you apply, plus tax filing and language and knowledge requirements where they apply.
Sources: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/eligibility/canadian-experience-class.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/proof-funds.html, https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/fees/fees.asp, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/check-score.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/canadian-citizenship/become-canadian-citizen/eligibility.html

## News
### Express Entry from 3 November 2026: extra CRS points for high-wage jobs, no LMIA for job offers (2026-10-21)
URL: https://riskllc.us/news/canada-express-entry-high-wage-points-3-november-2026.html
On 16 October 2026 IRCC announced that from 3 November 2026 Express Entry candidates get extra CRS points for Canadian work experience or a job offer in a high-wage occupation, and a job offer no longer needs an LMIA. Invitation rounds pause for up to two weeks while scores are recalculated.
Sources: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/2026/10/canada-refocusing-express-entry-on-top-talent-that-drives-economic-growth.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/2026/10/changes-to-express-entry-for-high-wage-occupations.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/check-score/high-wage.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/job-offer.html

### USA: no more automatic EAD extensions, DHS final rule in force from 14 October 2026 (2026-10-21)
URL: https://riskllc.us/news/us-ead-automatic-extension-ended-final-rule-october-2026.html
On 14 October 2026 DHS published a final rule confirming that work permits (EADs) are no longer automatically extended while a renewal is pending. Renewals filed on or after 30 October 2025 get no extension: the card expires on its printed date. File the renewal as soon as you are within 180 days of expiry.
Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/14/2026-20955/removal-of-automatic-extensions-for-certain-employment-authorization-documents, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/10/30/2025-19702/removal-of-the-automatic-extension-of-employment-authorization-documents, https://www.uscis.gov/newsroom/news-releases/dhs-ends-automatic-extension-of-employment-authorization, https://www.uscis.gov/green-card/green-card-processes-and-procedures/employment-authorization-document, https://www.uscis.gov/eadautoextend

### Proposal: USCIS wants to stop deferring to prior approvals when extending H-1B, L-1 and other work visas (2026-10-21)
URL: https://riskllc.us/news/uscis-proposes-ending-deference-extension-petitions-2026.html
On 14 October 2026 USCIS published a proposed rule to remove 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5), the regulation that tells officers to defer to an earlier approval when deciding an extension petition. It is only a proposal: comments are open until 13 November 2026, and nothing changes until a final rule is published.
Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/14/2026-20941/removing-deference-to-prior-uscis-determinations-of-eligibility, https://www.regulations.gov/docket/USCIS-2026-0529, https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-a-chapter-4, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/12/18/2024-29354/modernizing-h-1b-requirements-providing-flexibility-in-the-f-1-program-and-program-improvements

### New client results: UK visitor visa and Japan eVisa approved (2026-10-21)
URL: https://riskllc.us/news/client-results-uk-japan-visas-october-2026.html
On 19 October 2026 two RISK LLC clients from Uzbekistan received approvals: a UK Standard Visitor visa and a Japan temporary visitor eVisa.
Sources: https://www.gov.uk/standard-visitor, https://www.evisa.mofa.go.jp/

### DV-2027 green card lottery: court ordered registration (not open yet) (2026-10-16)
URL: https://riskllc.us/news/dv-2027-green-card-lottery-update.html
On October 14, 2026 Judge Jinsook Ohta ordered the State Department to run DV-2027. After a same-day joint modification, the department must announce by October 29 and open registration by November 1, 2026 (US Eastern), for 30 days. Registration is still not open.
Sources: https://www.courthousenews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/redeagle-v-rubio-ruling-101426.pdf, https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.casd.867598/gov.uscourts.casd.867598.23.0.pdf, https://www.courthousenews.com/trump-admin-ordered-to-reinstate-2027-green-card-lottery/, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/03/11/2026-04737/visas-enhancing-vetting-and-combatting-fraud-in-the-diversity-immigrant-visa-program, https://dvprogram.state.gov

### UK Student visa: money you must show rises from 30 November 2026 (2026-10-11)
URL: https://riskllc.us/news/uk-student-visa-maintenance-funds-30-november-2026.html
Under HC 584, UK Student visa applicants must show £1,570 a month in London and £1,203 a month outside London for applications made on or after 30 November 2026.
Sources: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/statement-of-changes-to-the-immigration-rules-hc-584-3-september-2026/statement-of-changes-to-the-immigration-rules-hc-584-3-september-2026-accessible, https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/statement-of-changes-to-the-immigration-rules-hc-584-3-september-2026/explanatory-memorandum-to-the-statement-of-changes-in-immigration-rules-hc-584-3-september-2026-accessible

### Explainer: how a Canada work permit works for applicants from Uzbekistan (2026-10-11)
URL: https://riskllc.us/news/canada-work-permit-explained-2026.html
Canada has two kinds of work permits, employer-specific and open. Most applicants from Uzbekistan need a job offer, pay CAD 155 plus CAD 85 biometrics, and can later move to PR and citizenship.
Sources: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/permit/temporary/eligibility.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/guide-5487-applying-work-permit-outside-canada.html, https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/fees/fees.asp, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/eligibility/canadian-experience-class.html, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/canadian-citizenship/become-canadian-citizen/eligibility.html
